promptPt: Quem escreveu a epopeia Os Lusíadas?
explanation: Camões wrote Os Lusíadas, the national epic, and is treated as the greatest poet of the Portuguese language. The national holiday on 10 June marks the day he died, in 1580. The other three writers are all famous, but they belong to much later periods.
source: Dossiê estado-cultura.md, secção 10.1; Presidência da República — Dia de Portugal.

promptPt: Em que ano foram publicados Os Lusíadas?
explanation: Os Lusíadas was published in 1572. Be careful with the nearby dates in the options: 1498 is Vasco da Gama reaching India and 1500 is Cabral reaching Brazil. Those are events the poem describes, not dates of publication.

promptPt: Quantos cantos têm Os Lusíadas?
explanation: The epic is organised in ten cantos. Twelve is the trap answer, because Virgil's Aeneid — the classical model Camões was working against — has twelve books, and he deliberately did not copy that.

promptPt: Que viagem serve de fio condutor a Os Lusíadas?
options: A viagem de Pedro Álvares Cabral ao Brasil
A conquista de Ceuta por D. João I
A primeira viagem à volta do mundo de Fernão de Magalhães
A viagem de Vasco da Gama à Índia
explanation: The poem follows Vasco da Gama's sea voyage to India and uses it as a frame to retell the whole history of Portugal. The other voyages listed are real and important, but none of them is the poem's narrative spine.

promptPt: Como se chama o gigante que, em Os Lusíadas, guarda o Cabo das Tormentas?
explanation: Adamastor is the giant who rises out of the sea at the Cape of Good Hope (then called Cabo das Tormentas) and threatens the sailors. He is one of the most quoted images in Portuguese literature. Baco and Netuno do appear in the poem, but as classical gods, not as the cape's guardian.

promptPt: Em Os Lusíadas, que personagem critica a aventura marítima no momento da partida?
explanation: The Velho do Restelo is an old man on the quayside who denounces the voyage as vanity and greed. He matters because he shows the poem is not simple propaganda — Camões gives the critics a voice. Restelo is the Lisbon riverside area next to today's Belém.

promptPt: Onde se encontra o túmulo simbólico de Luís Vaz de Camões?
options: No Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, em Lisboa
No Convento de Cristo, em Tomar
explanation: Camões has a symbolic tomb in the Jerónimos Monastery in Belém, facing Vasco da Gama's — poet and navigator side by side. It is called symbolic because his actual remains were lost. The Panteão Nacional is where Amália Rodrigues is buried, which is a common mix-up.

promptPt: Que data assinala o Dia de Portugal, de Camões e das Comunidades Portuguesas?
explanation: The national day is 10 June, the date Camões died in 1580, and its full official name includes both Camões and the Portuguese communities abroad. The other three dates are also national holidays, but they mark the 1974 revolution, the 1910 Republic and the 1640 Restoration.
source: Presidência da República — Dia de Portugal; estado-cultura.md 5.3.

promptPt: O que criou Fernando Pessoa, e que se tornou a marca da sua obra?
options: Um novo alfabeto para a língua portuguesa
Heterónimos — poetas imaginários com biografia e estilo próprios
explanation: Pessoa invented heteronyms: whole imaginary poets, each with a life story, a personality and a distinct style. This is not the same as a pen name, because the heteronyms argue with one another in print. It is the single most-tested fact about him.

promptPt: Quais são os três principais heterónimos de Fernando Pessoa?
options: Alberto Caeiro, Ricardo Reis e Álvaro de Campos
Bernardo Soares, Ricardo Reis e Mário de Sá-Carneiro
Alberto Caeiro, António Nobre e Almada Negreiros
Álvaro de Campos, Cesário Verde e Camilo Pessanha
explanation: The big three are Caeiro (the plain, pastoral "master"), Reis (classical odes) and Campos (loud and modern). Bernardo Soares exists but is classed as a semi-heteronym. The other names in the wrong options are real Portuguese writers, not Pessoa's inventions.

promptPt: Qual é o único livro de poesia em português que Fernando Pessoa publicou em vida?
explanation: Mensagem came out in 1934, one year before Pessoa died, and was the only Portuguese-language poetry book he published while alive. Almost everything else was found afterwards in a trunk of manuscripts, including the Livro do Desassossego.

promptPt: A que semi-heterónimo é atribuído o Livro do Desassossego?
explanation: The Book of Disquiet is signed by Bernardo Soares, called a semi-heteronym because he stands close to Pessoa himself rather than being a fully separate figure. It was assembled from loose papers and published decades after Pessoa's death.

promptPt: Que escritor de língua portuguesa recebeu o Prémio Nobel da Literatura?
explanation: Saramago won the Nobel Prize in Literature in 1998 and remains the only Portuguese-language writer to have done so. He was born in Azinhaga, in the Golegã area, and died in Lanzarote in 2010.
source: estado-cultura.md 10.3 (com a ressalva de verificação da secção 12).

promptPt: Qual destas obras é de José Saramago?
explanation: Memorial do Convento is Saramago's, built around the construction of the Mafra palace-convent. Os Maias and A Cidade e as Serras are Eça de Queirós; Mensagem is Pessoa. Saramago's other best-known titles are Ensaio sobre a Cegueira and O Ano da Morte de Ricardo Reis.

promptPt: Quem escreveu Os Maias, o grande romance do realismo português?
explanation: Eça de Queirós (1845-1900) is the great realist novelist, and Os Maias and O Primo Basílio are his best-known books. Garrett and Camilo Castelo Branco belong to the earlier Romantic generation, and Agustina Bessa-Luís is a 20th-century novelist.

promptPt: Em que ano é que a UNESCO inscreveu o fado na Lista Representativa do Património Cultural Imaterial da Humanidade?
explanation: Fado was inscribed on UNESCO's Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2011. "Intangible" heritage means living practices and expressions rather than buildings, which is why fado sits on a different list from the Jerónimos Monastery.
source: UNESCO — Fado, urban popular song of Portugal (2011); estado-cultura.md 10.4.

promptPt: Que instrumento acompanha tipicamente o fado, a par da viola?
explanation: Fado is normally sung solo, accompanied by a guitarra portuguesa plus a viola, which is what a standard classical guitar is called in this context. The guitarra portuguesa is pear-shaped and found nowhere else. The cavaquinho and the accordion belong to folk music, not to fado.

promptPt: Quantas cordas tem a guitarra portuguesa?
explanation: The Portuguese guitar has twelve steel strings, arranged in six pairs, on a pear-shaped body. Six strings would make it an ordinary guitar and four would make it a cavaquinho, so the number is what identifies the instrument.

promptPt: De que palavra latina vem a palavra «fado»?
explanation: "Fado" comes from the Latin fatum, meaning fate or destiny, which explains the resigned mood of the songs. This also helps you remember that in everyday Portuguese "o fado" can still mean somebody's fate or lot in life.

promptPt: Quem é conhecida como a «rainha do fado»?
explanation: Amália Rodrigues (1920-1999) is the queen of fado and the voice that carried the genre around the world. Mariza and Ana Moura are later fado singers. Sophia de Mello Breyner Andresen is a poet, not a singer, which makes that option a deliberate trap.

promptPt: Onde está sepultada Amália Rodrigues?
explanation: Amália rests in the Panteão Nacional, the church of Santa Engrácia in Lisbon, which holds figures the country chose to honour. Do not confuse it with the Jerónimos Monastery, where Camões and Vasco da Gama have their tombs.

promptPt: Qual é a diferença principal entre o fado de Coimbra e o fado de Lisboa?
options: O fado de Coimbra canta-se sem qualquer instrumento
O fado de Coimbra canta-se em latim
O fado de Coimbra é anterior ao século XV
O fado de Coimbra está ligado à Universidade e é cantado por homens, de capa e batina
explanation: Coimbra fado grew out of student life at the university, is traditionally sung by men wearing the black academic cape, and is often performed outdoors as a serenade. Lisbon fado was born in the city's working-class districts in the 19th century and is sung by women and men alike.

promptPt: Que sentimento é considerado o centro do fado?
explanation: Saudade is the missing of someone or something, felt with affection and with no exact English translation. It is the emotional core of fado and a word you will hear constantly in daily life — "tenho saudades tuas" means roughly "I miss you".

promptPt: Qual é o peixe considerado o prato nacional de Portugal, com centenas de receitas diferentes?
explanation: Bacalhau, salt cod, is the national dish, and people say there are over a thousand ways to cook it. Well-known versions are bacalhau à Brás, com natas and à Gomes de Sá, plus pastéis de bacalhau. Fresh fish is eaten too, but cod is the cultural icon.

promptPt: O que é preciso fazer ao bacalhau salgado e seco antes de o cozinhar?
options: Demolhá-lo em água, mudando a água várias vezes
Assá-lo na brasa sem qualquer preparação
explanation: Salted dried cod has to be soaked in cold water, with several changes of water, usually for a day or more depending on thickness. Skip this and the fish is inedibly salty. Supermarkets also sell it ready-soaked, labelled "demolhado".

promptPt: Que ingredientes leva o caldo verde?
explanation: Caldo verde is a soup of finely shredded couve, a kale-like cabbage, with potato, olive oil and a slice of chouriço sausage. It comes from the Minho in the north but is eaten all over the country, especially at festivals and weddings.

promptPt: Como se chama o doce português mais conhecido, cuja versão original é feita em Lisboa desde 1837?
options: O pastel de nata — na versão original, o pastel de Belém
explanation: The custard tart is the best-known Portuguese pastry. The original, made in Belém since 1837, is the only one that may carry the name "pastel de Belém"; everywhere else it is a "pastel de nata". Having one with a bica is a national habit.

promptPt: De que região vem o vinho do Porto?
explanation: Port is made from grapes grown on the terraced slopes of the Douro valley and was traditionally aged in Vila Nova de Gaia, across the river from Porto. It is a fortified wine, meaning grape spirit is added during fermentation. Vinho verde, by contrast, comes from the Minho.
source: estado-cultura.md 10.5; IVDP — Região Demarcada do Douro.

promptPt: Em que ano foi criada a Região Demarcada do Douro, considerada a primeira região vitícola demarcada e regulamentada do mundo?
explanation: In 1756, under King José I and his minister the Marquês de Pombal, the Companhia Geral da Agricultura das Vinhas do Alto Douro was created and the Douro was demarcated and regulated. Earlier demarcations existed elsewhere, but the Douro was the first with a full regulatory and classification system. The same Pombal rebuilt Lisbon after the 1755 earthquake.
source: IVDP — A Região Demarcada do Douro; IVV — Douro/Porto; historia.md 5.

promptPt: De que região é típico o vinho verde?
explanation: Vinho verde comes from the Minho, in the far north-west. "Verde" refers to how young the wine is drunk, not to its colour — there are white, red and rosé versions. It is light, faintly sparkling and low in alcohol.

promptPt: Portugal é o maior produtor mundial de que matéria-prima, extraída sobretudo no Alentejo?
explanation: Portugal is the world's largest producer of cork, stripped from sobreiros (cork oaks) mostly in the Alentejo. A cork oak is only stripped every nine years and the tree is never felled to harvest it. Portugal produces plenty of olive oil, salt and marble too, but is not the world leader in those.

promptPt: Qual é o queijo português mais famoso e de que leite é feito?
options: Queijo da Ilha, de leite de vaca
Queijo de Azeitão, de leite de cabra
Queijo Serra da Estrela, de leite de ovelha
Queijo de Nisa, de leite de vaca
explanation: Serra da Estrela is the most famous Portuguese cheese and it is made from sheep's milk, curdled with thistle flower, which gives it a soft centre you eat with a spoon. Read the options carefully: Azeitão and Nisa are also sheep's-milk cheeses, so those options are wrong on the milk, not on the name.

promptPt: Como se chama, em Lisboa, o café curto que noutros países se chama expresso?
explanation: In Lisbon a short black coffee is a "bica"; in Porto the same drink is often called a "cimbalino". A galão is coffee with a lot of milk in a tall glass, a garoto is an espresso with a little milk, and an abatanado is longer and weaker. If you simply ask for "um café", you get an espresso.

promptPt: Em que altura do ano se comem sobretudo sardinhas assadas?
options: Em junho, nas festas dos santos populares
explanation: Grilled sardines belong to June, when the santos populares fill the streets — Santo António in Lisbon on 13 June and São João in Porto on 24 June. Sardines are at their fattest and best in summer. Christmas Eve dinner, the consoada, is traditionally boiled salt cod with cabbage and potatoes instead.

promptPt: Com que país faz Portugal fronteira terrestre?
options: Não faz fronteira terrestre com nenhum país
explanation: Portugal's only land border is with Spain. It is one of the oldest borders in Europe, largely fixed by the Treaty of Alcanices in 1297. Everything else is Atlantic coastline, which is why the sea runs through so much of the country's history and food.

promptPt: Qual é o rio mais longo da Península Ibérica, que desagua em Lisboa?
explanation: The Tejo (Tagus) is the longest river on the Iberian Peninsula. It rises in Spain and reaches the sea at Lisbon, where it widens into a huge estuary. The Douro also rises in Spain, but it meets the Atlantic at Porto instead.

promptPt: Que rio desagua no Porto e dá nome à região vinhateira classificada pela UNESCO?
explanation: The Douro meets the Atlantic at Porto, and its terraced upper valley is the Alto Douro Vinhateiro, a UNESCO World Heritage cultural landscape. Those terraces produce port wine. The Minho is further north and marks the border with Spain.

promptPt: Qual é o rio mais longo inteiramente português?
explanation: The Mondego is the longest river that runs entirely inside Portugal, from the Serra da Estrela to the sea at Figueira da Foz, passing through Coimbra on the way. The Tejo and the Douro are longer overall but both rise in Spain. Longest river versus longest entirely Portuguese river is a classic exam trap.

promptPt: Qual é o ponto mais alto de Portugal continental?
options: A Torre, na Serra da Estrela, com 1993 metros
explanation: The Torre, in the Serra da Estrela, is the highest point of mainland Portugal at 1,993 metres. Watch the wording of the question: the highest point of all Portuguese territory is Mount Pico in the Azores. Pico Ruivo is Madeira's highest peak and Cabo da Roca is a sea cliff.

promptPt: Qual é o ponto mais alto de todo o território português?
options: A Torre, na Serra da Estrela
A Montanha do Pico, nos Açores, com 2351 metros
explanation: Mount Pico, on Pico island in the Azores, is a volcano 2,351 metres high and the highest point in the whole country. The Torre is only the highest point of the mainland. Whenever a question says "de todo o território português", the answer is in the Azores.

promptPt: Que cabo, no concelho de Sintra, é o ponto mais ocidental da Europa continental?
explanation: Cabo da Roca, in Sintra, is the westernmost point of mainland Europe. Cabo de São Vicente is the south-western tip, down in the Algarve, and is the option most often confused with it. Cabo Espichel and Cabo Carvoeiro are on the coast near Setúbal and Peniche.

promptPt: Quantas ilhas tem o arquipélago dos Açores?
explanation: The Azores have nine islands, in three groups: Western (Flores, Corvo), Central (Faial, Pico, São Jorge, Graciosa, Terceira) and Eastern (São Miguel, Santa Maria). Learning the three groups is the easiest way to remember the total.

promptPt: Qual é a maior ilha dos Açores?
explanation: São Miguel is the largest Azorean island and home to Ponta Delgada, the archipelago's biggest city. Terceira has the historic city of Angra do Heroísmo, a UNESCO site, and Pico has the country's highest mountain — each island tends to have its own claim to fame.

promptPt: Qual é a capital da Região Autónoma da Madeira?
explanation: Funchal is Madeira's capital. Ponta Delgada and Angra do Heroísmo are both in the Azores, so they are there to catch you out. Porto Santo is the second inhabited island of the Madeira archipelago, alongside the uninhabited Desertas and Selvagens.

promptPt: Quais são as duas regiões autónomas de Portugal?
explanation: The Azores and Madeira are the two autonomous regions, each with its own Legislative Assembly and Regional Government, plus a Representative of the Republic appointed by the President. The Algarve and the Alentejo are mainland regions with no autonomous status, and Macau was handed to China in 1999.

promptPt: Em quantos distritos está dividido Portugal continental?
explanation: Mainland Portugal has 18 districts, running from Viana do Castelo in the north to Faro in the south. The autonomous regions are not divided into districts. Do not confuse the 18 districts with the 308 municipalities.

promptPt: Quantos municípios (concelhos) tem Portugal?
explanation: Portugal has 308 municipalities: 278 on the mainland, 19 in the Azores and 11 in Madeira. Every distractor here is a real Portuguese number — 18 districts, 230 members of parliament, and around three thousand freguesias — so read which unit the question is asking about.

promptPt: Qual é o único parque nacional de Portugal?
options: O Parque Natural da Serra da Estrela
O Parque Natural do Sudoeste Alentejano
explanation: Peneda-Gerês, in the far north near the Spanish border, is Portugal's only parque nacional. Everything else in the options is a parque natural, which is a different and lower level of protection. The word "nacional" is exactly what this question tests.

promptPt: Qual é a segunda maior cidade de Portugal?
explanation: Porto is the second city, sitting at the mouth of the Douro in the north. Lisbon is the capital and the largest city. Porto gave its name to port wine, and its historic centre is on the UNESCO World Heritage list.

promptPt: Que rio marca a fronteira norte entre Portugal e Espanha?
explanation: The Minho marks the northern border with Spain and gives its name to the province around it. The Guadiana marks part of the eastern and southern border, in the Alentejo and Algarve. The Mondego runs entirely inside Portugal and touches no border at all.

promptPt: Como se caracteriza o clima de Portugal?
options: Mediterrânico, com verões quentes e secos e invernos suaves e chuvosos
Tropical, quente e húmido durante todo o ano
Continental, com invernos muito frios e secos
Polar, com neve durante a maior parte do ano
explanation: Portugal has a Mediterranean climate: hot dry summers and mild rainy winters. Within that, the north is noticeably wetter and greener and the south, especially the Alentejo and Algarve, is drier and hotter. Most rain falls between October and March.

promptPt: Aproximadamente quantas pessoas residiam em Portugal no final de 2025?
explanation: The INE, the national statistics institute, counted 11,424,031 residents on 31 December 2025. The median age was 45.8 years, which tells you Portugal is an ageing country. Note that Portuguese uses a comma as the decimal separator: 11,4 milhões.
source: INE — Estimativas de População Residente 2025; estado-cultura.md 8.

promptPt: Em que concelho fica Santa Cruz, a zona costeira a norte de Lisboa?
explanation: Santa Cruz is a coastal area in the municipality of Torres Vedras, in the Lisbon district. Knowing your own concelho matters in practice, because that is where the Câmara Municipal and your Junta de Freguesia handle your paperwork.

promptPt: Como se chama a arte decorativa, em placas de cerâmica pintada, que cobre igrejas, palácios e estações de comboio em Portugal?
explanation: Azulejos are the painted ceramic tiles that cover walls all over Portugal, very often in blue and white, and they are considered the country's most characteristic decorative art. Calçada portuguesa is the other great everyday art form, but it is under your feet rather than on the walls.

promptPt: O que é a calçada portuguesa?
options: O pavimento de pedra preta e branca dos passeios e das praças
Um tipo de calçado tradicional do Minho
explanation: Calçada portuguesa is the black-and-white stone paving that covers pavements and squares across the country, laid by hand in patterns by a craftsman called a calceteiro. The wave design in Lisbon's Rossio is the most famous example. Note the European Portuguese word "passeio" for pavement.

promptPt: Quantos bens portugueses estão inscritos na Lista do Património Mundial da UNESCO?
explanation: UNESCO lists 17 World Heritage properties for Portugal. They include the Jerónimos Monastery and Tower of Belém, the monasteries of Batalha and Alcobaça, the Convent of Christ in Tomar, the historic centres of Évora, Guimarães, Porto and Angra do Heroísmo, the Sintra cultural landscape, the Alto Douro, the University of Coimbra and Madeira's Laurissilva forest.
source: UNESCO — página de país de Portugal (17 sítios); estado-cultura.md 10.6.

promptPt: Que cidade é conhecida como o «berço da nação»?
explanation: Guimarães is called the cradle of the nation because it is tied to Afonso Henriques, the first king, and the Battle of São Mamede was fought nearby in 1128. Its historic centre is a UNESCO World Heritage site. Coimbra and Lisbon were later capitals of the kingdom.

promptPt: Em que dia se celebra Santo António, o santo popular de Lisboa?
explanation: Santo António is celebrated in Lisbon on 13 June, with street parties, grilled sardines and the marchas populares down the Avenida da Liberdade. The 24th is São João in Porto. The 10th is the national day, which is a completely different occasion — do not let the same month confuse you.

promptPt: Em que cidade se celebra o São João a 24 de junho?
explanation: São João is Porto's big night, on 24 June, famous for grilled sardines, plastic hammers and small hot-air balloons. Together with Santo António in Lisbon these are the santos populares, the June street festivals. Braga also has well-known São João celebrations, but Porto is the standard answer.

promptPt: Qual é o maior centro de peregrinação religiosa de Portugal?
explanation: Fátima, in the municipality of Ourém, is the country's main pilgrimage site, and the biggest gatherings are on 13 May and 13 October. Portugal is Roman Catholic by majority tradition, but the State itself is secular and religious freedom is complete under Article 41 of the Constitution.

promptPt: Qual é o desporto mais popular em Portugal e quais são os três grandes clubes?
options: O futebol — Benfica, Sporting CP e FC Porto
O andebol — Sporting CP, ABC e Benfica
O ciclismo — Boavista, Vitória e Braga
O hóquei em patins — FC Porto, Benfica e Oliveirense
explanation: Football is by far the most popular sport, and the "três grandes" are Benfica and Sporting from Lisbon plus FC Porto. Note two European Portuguese words you will need: "desporto" for sport and "equipa" for team. The national side won the Euro in 2016 and the Nations League in 2019 and 2025.

promptPt: Que carnaval é tradicionalmente descrito como «o mais português de Portugal»?
explanation: The Torres Vedras carnival is known for its satire of politics and public life, and is traditionally billed as the most Portuguese carnival in the country. Loulé, Ovar and Sesimbra also hold big, long-established carnivals. Carnival falls in February or March, because its date depends on Easter.

promptPt: Para onde emigraram, em grande número, os portugueses ao longo do século XX?
options: Sobretudo para a Rússia e a Polónia
Sobretudo para a Austrália e a Nova Zelândia
Sobretudo para a Índia e o Japão
Sobretudo para França, o Luxemburgo, a Suíça, o Brasil, os Estados Unidos e o Canadá
explanation: Emigration shaped 20th-century Portugal, leaving very large communities in France, Luxembourg, Switzerland, Brazil, the United States and Canada. That is why the national day is officially also the day "das Comunidades Portuguesas", and why Parliament has two constituencies for citizens living abroad.

promptPt: Quantos feriados obrigatórios existem em Portugal, segundo o Código do Trabalho?
explanation: The Labour Code sets 13 obligatory public holidays. Three of them move each year because they are tied to Easter. Beyond these 13, the Code also allows two further days to be observed — the local municipal holiday and Carnival Tuesday — but those are not obligatory everywhere.
source: Código do Trabalho, artigo 234.º (ver nota de lacunas nas Fontes).

promptPt: Quais destes feriados portugueses mudam de data todos os anos?
options: 25 de abril, 1 de maio e 10 de junho
A Sexta-feira Santa, o Domingo de Páscoa e o Corpo de Deus
15 de agosto, 5 de outubro e 1 de novembro
1 de dezembro, 8 de dezembro e 25 de dezembro
explanation: Three obligatory holidays are movable because they follow Easter: Good Friday, Easter Sunday and Corpus Christi. All the others fall on fixed calendar dates. Carnival is also tied to Easter, but it is not one of the obligatory holidays.

promptPt: O que se celebra a 25 de abril?
options: O Dia da Liberdade, aniversário da Revolução dos Cravos de 1974
explanation: 25 April is Liberdade Day, marking the 1974 Carnation Revolution that ended the Estado Novo dictatorship almost without bloodshed. The Constitution now in force came into effect on 25 April 1976, exactly two years later. Lisbon's long bridge over the Tejo carries the same name.

promptPt: O que se celebra a 5 de outubro?
explanation: 5 October marks the proclamation of the Republic in 1910, when the monarchy ended and King Manuel II left for exile. Here is a curiosity worth knowing: 5 October 1143 is also the traditional date of the meeting at Zamora, so the same day carries two very different anniversaries.

promptPt: O que se celebra a 1 de dezembro?
explanation: 1 December marks the 1640 restoration of independence, which ended sixty years of Spanish kings ruling Portugal. The Duke of Bragança was acclaimed King João IV two weeks later. The war that followed lasted 28 years and ended only with the Treaty of Lisbon in 1668.

promptPt: O que se celebra a 1 de maio?
explanation: 1 May is Labour Day and an obligatory public holiday. It was first celebrated in freedom in 1974, days after the Carnation Revolution, and images of that day are part of how Portugal remembers the return of democracy. Mother's Day is also in May, but it falls on a Sunday and is not a holiday.

promptPt: Além dos feriados obrigatórios, que outro dia pode ser observado como feriado em cada concelho?
options: Um feriado regional decidido pelo Governo
Um feriado escolar fixado por cada escola
explanation: Beyond the 13 obligatory holidays, the Labour Code allows the local municipal holiday and Carnival Tuesday to be observed as well. Because they are permitted rather than required, whether you actually get the day off depends on your employer or collective agreement. Lisbon's municipal day is 13 June and Porto's is 24 June.
source: Código do Trabalho, artigo 234.º; estado-cultura.md 10.6 (ver nota de lacunas).

promptPt: Por quantas pessoas, aproximadamente, é falada a língua portuguesa no mundo?
explanation: Portuguese is spoken by over 250 million people across four continents and is the official language of nine countries. That is the reason the CPLP, the community of Portuguese-speaking countries, exists at all. Note that European Portuguese says "mil milhões" where Brazilians say "bilhão".

promptPt: Quantos Estados-membros tem a CPLP?
explanation: The CPLP has nine member states: Angola, Brazil, Cape Verde, Guinea-Bissau, Equatorial Guinea, Mozambique, Portugal, São Tomé and Príncipe, and Timor-Leste. It was founded in Lisbon on 17 July 1996 by seven of them, with Timor-Leste and Equatorial Guinea joining later.

promptPt: No processo de nacionalidade, de que é que se presume que os nacionais dos países de língua oficial portuguesa estão dispensados?
options: De todo o teste de nacionalidade
Apenas da parte da língua — não da cultura, da história nem dos símbolos nacionais
explanation: Article 6(10) of Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026 presumes that nationals of Portuguese-speaking countries meet only the first part of requirement (c), which is the language. Culture, history, national symbols and the civic knowledge in requirement (d) are not covered, so Brazilians, Angolans, Cape Verdeans and others still have to show that knowledge. The presumption can also be rebutted if a lack of Portuguese is obvious.
source: Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, artigo 6.º, n.º 10 (citado verbatim em historia.md); estado-cultura.md 7.

promptPt: Qual é a religião de tradição maioritária em Portugal e qual é a posição do Estado?
options: Católica — e o catolicismo é a religião oficial do Estado
Protestante — e o Estado é confessional
Católica romana na tradição maioritária — mas o Estado é laico e há plena liberdade religiosa
Não há tradição religiosa maioritária e a religião é proibida no espaço público
explanation: Most of Portugal is Roman Catholic by tradition, which shows in the calendar and in local festivals. But the State is secular: Article 41 of the Constitution guarantees freedom of conscience, religion and worship, and the State professes no religion. There is no official State church.

promptPt: Que direito garante a Constituição a todos, através de um Serviço Nacional de Saúde?
options: O direito à proteção da saúde, através de um SNS universal e tendencialmente gratuito
O direito a tratamento apenas em hospitais privados
O direito a cuidados de saúde só para cidadãos portugueses
O direito a um seguro de saúde privado pago pelo Estado
explanation: The Constitution guarantees the right to health protection through a universal National Health Service that is "tendencialmente gratuito" — largely free, with small charges called taxas moderadoras. Under Article 15, foreigners resident in Portugal generally have the same rights and duties as Portuguese citizens, with political rights as the main exception. In practice you register at your local centro de saúde to get a número de utente.

promptPt: Que percentagem da população residente em Portugal era, aproximadamente, de nacionalidade estrangeira no final de 2025?
explanation: About 1.6 million of the 11.4 million residents at the end of 2025 were foreign nationals, roughly 14%. Portugal has changed quickly: for most of the 20th century it sent people abroad, and it is now also a country of immigration. A median age of 45.8 explains why that shift matters demographically.
source: INE — Estimativas de População Residente 2025; estado-cultura.md 8.

promptPt: Em Portugal, votar é obrigatório?
options: Sim, e quem não vota paga uma multa
Não — votar é um dever cívico, mas o voto não é obrigatório
Sim, mas apenas nas eleições presidenciais
Não existe direito de voto em Portugal
explanation: Voting is described as a civic duty, but it is not compulsory and there is no fine for abstaining. Keep the right and the duty separate in your mind: whether a foreign resident may vote at all depends on nationality and on reciprocity rules, so check your own situation rather than assuming.

promptPt: Como se organizam habitualmente as refeições, num dia típico em Portugal?
options: Pequeno-almoço às 10h, almoço às 16h e jantar às 23h
Apenas duas refeições: almoço e jantar
Pequeno-almoço cedo, almoço por volta das 13h e jantar por volta das 20h
Pequeno-almoço às 6h, almoço às 11h e jantar às 17h
explanation: A typical Portuguese day has an early, light pequeno-almoço, lunch around 1 p.m. and dinner around 8 p.m., often later in summer. Lunch is usually the bigger meal, and many restaurants serve a fixed "prato do dia". Note the European Portuguese word: "pequeno-almoço", never the Brazilian "café da manhã".

promptPt: Qual é a forma de governo de Portugal?
explanation: Portugal is a semi-presidential republic: there is a directly elected President as head of state, and separately a Prime Minister and Government that answer to Parliament. The monarchy ended in 1910, and Portugal is a unitary state, not a federal one.
source: Constituição da República Portuguesa (CRP), arts. 1.º e 110.º; dossiê `content/civica/estado-cultura.md` §1.

promptPt: Quais são os quatro órgãos de soberania previstos na Constituição?
options: O Presidente da República, a Assembleia da República, o Governo e os Tribunais
A Assembleia da República, o Governo, o Provedor de Justiça e os Tribunais
O Presidente da República, o Governo, as autarquias locais e os Tribunais
O Presidente da República, o Conselho de Estado, o Governo e os Tribunais
explanation: Article 110 of the Constitution lists exactly four organs of sovereignty, and this is one of the most predictable civics questions you will meet. The Council of State and the Ombudsman matter, but neither is an organ of sovereignty. Local authorities are not organs of sovereignty either.

promptPt: Quantos são os órgãos de soberania da República Portuguesa?
explanation: There are four. If you are used to the classic "three branches" idea, note that Portugal splits the executive in two: the President and the Government are separate organs of sovereignty.

promptPt: Em que ano foi aprovada a Constituição da República Portuguesa atualmente em vigor?
explanation: The current Constitution was approved by the Constituent Assembly on 2 April 1976. 1974 is the year of the revolution, not of the Constitution, and 1933 is the constitution of the Estado Novo dictatorship.
source: CRP, texto aprovado a 2 de abril de 1976 (parlamento.pt); dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §1.

promptPt: A Constituição de 1976 resultou diretamente de que acontecimento?
options: Da implantação da República, a 5 de outubro de 1910
Da Revolução de 25 de abril de 1974
Da adesão de Portugal à Comunidade Económica Europeia
explanation: The Carnation Revolution of 25 April 1974 ended nearly 48 years of dictatorship (the Estado Novo). A Constituent Assembly was then elected, and it wrote the Constitution that is still in force.

promptPt: Quantas revisões constitucionais teve já a Constituição de 1976?
explanation: There have been seven constitutional revisions, and the most recent dates from 2005. A useful pairing to memorise: approved 1976, last revised 2005.
source: Assembleia da República — CRP, VII Revisão Constitucional (2005); dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §1.

promptPt: Segundo o artigo 2.º da Constituição, Portugal é...
explanation: Article 2 defines Portugal as a democratic state governed by the rule of law. This exact phrase matters for citizenship applicants: the law requires you to declare solemnly your adherence to the fundamental principles of the "Estado de direito democrático".
source: CRP, art. 2.º; Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, art. 6.º n.º 1 al. e); dossiês `estado-cultura.md` §1 e `regulamento.md` §3.

promptPt: Quem é o Chefe de Estado em Portugal?
options: O Presidente da Assembleia da República
O Presidente do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça
explanation: The President of the Republic is the head of state and represents the Republic. The Prime Minister is head of government — a different job. Keep the two apart; questions often try to confuse them.

promptPt: Quanto tempo dura o mandato do Presidente da República?
explanation: The presidential term is five years. Do not confuse it with the four-year term of members of Parliament and of local councils.

promptPt: Quantos mandatos consecutivos pode cumprir, no máximo, o Presidente da República?
explanation: The President may be re-elected once, so the maximum is two consecutive five-year terms — ten years. Marcelo Rebelo de Sousa served exactly that, from 2016 to 2026.

promptPt: Qual é a idade mínima para ser eleito Presidente da República?
explanation: Article 122 sets the minimum age at 35. Compare it with the voting age of 18 — the two numbers are often tested together.

promptPt: Quem pode ser eleito Presidente da República?
options: Qualquer cidadão residente em Portugal há mais de dez anos
Qualquer cidadão da União Europeia recenseado em Portugal
Qualquer cidadão português, incluindo os naturalizados
Apenas um cidadão português de origem, com mais de 35 anos e no gozo dos seus direitos civis e políticos
explanation: Only a Portuguese citizen "de origem" — by origin, not by naturalisation — may become President. This is one of the few places where the Constitution treats naturalised citizens differently from citizens by origin.

promptPt: Como é eleito o Presidente da República?
options: Por sufrágio universal, direto e secreto de todos os cidadãos eleitores
Pela Assembleia da República, por maioria de dois terços
Pelo Conselho de Estado, sob proposta do Governo
Por um colégio eleitoral formado pelos presidentes de câmara
explanation: The President is elected directly by the citizens, in a universal and secret ballot. This direct election is what makes the system semi-presidential rather than parliamentary.

promptPt: O que acontece se, na eleição presidencial, nenhum candidato obtiver mais de metade dos votos?
options: Realiza-se uma segunda volta entre os dois candidatos mais votados
A Assembleia da República escolhe entre os dois mais votados
É eleito o candidato mais votado na primeira volta
Repete-se toda a eleição, com novas candidaturas
explanation: Portugal uses a two-round system: an absolute majority is needed to win outright, otherwise the top two candidates face a run-off. António José Seguro was elected in exactly such a run-off, on 8 February 2026.

promptPt: Qual destas competências NÃO pertence ao Presidente da República?
explanation: The state budget is approved by Parliament, not by the President. The President's toolkit is appointing, promulgating, vetoing, referring laws to the Constitutional Court and dissolving Parliament.

promptPt: Quem é o Comandante Supremo das Forças Armadas?
options: O Chefe do Estado-Maior-General das Forças Armadas
explanation: The President is Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces. It is a constitutional title that goes with being head of state; day-to-day military administration belongs to the Government.

promptPt: Como se chama o órgão político de consulta do Presidente da República?
options: O Conselho Superior de Defesa Nacional
explanation: The Council of State (Conselho de Estado) advises the President. Do not mix it up with the Council of Ministers, which is the Government's collective body chaired by the Prime Minister.

promptPt: Qual é a residência oficial do Presidente da República?
explanation: The President's official residence is the Palácio de Belém in Lisbon. The Palácio de São Bento houses Parliament — and the Prime Minister's official residence stands in its grounds.

promptPt: Quantos deputados tem a Assembleia da República?
explanation: The Constitution allows between 181 and 230 MPs, and the electoral law fixes the number at 230. In practice you should simply remember 230.
source: CRP, art. 148.º; Assembleia da República — deputados em funções, XVII Legislatura; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §2.2 e §3.

promptPt: Por quanto tempo são eleitos os deputados à Assembleia da República?
explanation: MPs are elected for four years, forming a "legislatura". Five years is the President's term — keep the two figures separate.

promptPt: Que método é usado para converter votos em mandatos nas eleições legislativas portuguesas?
options: O sistema maioritário a uma volta
A representação proporcional, pelo método de Hondt
Um sistema misto, com metade dos lugares por círculo uninominal
explanation: Portugal uses proportional representation with the d'Hondt method, applied to closed party lists in multi-member constituencies. That is why small parties can win seats without ever coming first anywhere.

promptPt: Onde reúne a Assembleia da República?
options: No Palácio de Belém, em Lisboa
No Palácio da Bolsa, no Porto
No Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, em Lisboa
No Palácio de São Bento, em Lisboa
explanation: Parliament sits at the Palácio de São Bento in Lisbon. If you hear "São Bento" in the news about a political decision, it usually means Parliament or the Prime Minister's office.

promptPt: Qual destas funções pertence à Assembleia da República?
options: Aprovar o Orçamento do Estado e fiscalizar o Governo
Julgar os crimes cometidos por membros do Governo
Nomear os presidentes de câmara municipal
explanation: Parliament legislates, approves the state budget, scrutinises the Government and may pass motions of censure. It does not appoint the President — voters do — and it does not try criminal cases; that is the courts' work.

promptPt: Perante quem responde politicamente o Governo?
explanation: The Government is politically accountable to Parliament, which can bring it down with a motion of censure. The President appoints the Prime Minister but cannot dismiss the Government simply for political disagreement.

promptPt: Quem nomeia o Primeiro-Ministro?
options: O Presidente da República, ouvidos os partidos e tendo em conta os resultados eleitorais
O partido mais votado nas eleições legislativas
A Assembleia da República, por votação
explanation: The President appoints the Prime Minister after consulting the parties in Parliament and in the light of the election results. There is no investiture vote in Parliament — but the new Government must survive its programme's scrutiny there.

promptPt: Quem nomeia os ministros e os secretários de Estado?
options: A Assembleia da República, por maioria simples
O Conselho de Ministros, por deliberação
O Presidente da República, sob proposta do Primeiro-Ministro
explanation: Formally the President appoints them, but only on the Prime Minister's proposal — so the choice is the Prime Minister's and the act is the President's. This shared step is typical of a semi-presidential system.

promptPt: Como se chama o órgão colegial do Governo?
explanation: The Council of Ministers is the Government's collegiate body, chaired by the Prime Minister. Decree-laws are approved there, which is why its weekly communiqué is where new legislation is first announced.

promptPt: Quem substitui o Presidente da República em caso de impedimento temporário?
options: O Presidente da Assembleia da República
O Presidente do Supremo Tribunal de Justiça
O membro mais antigo do Conselho de Estado
explanation: The Speaker of Parliament stands in for the President when the office is vacant or the President is unable to act. That is one reason the Speaker's election, by absolute majority at the first plenary sitting, matters so much.

promptPt: Em nome de quem administram a justiça os tribunais portugueses?
options: Em nome do Presidente da República
Em nome da Assembleia da República
explanation: The Constitution says the courts administer justice "em nome do povo" — in the name of the people. They are independent and subject only to the law, and trials are public unless the law says otherwise.

promptPt: Qual é o tribunal competente para apreciar a constitucionalidade das leis?
explanation: The Constitutional Court rules on whether laws comply with the Constitution. The President can refer a law to it before promulgating — this is called "fiscalização preventiva".

promptPt: Que tribunal fiscaliza a legalidade das despesas públicas?
explanation: The Tribunal de Contas — the Court of Auditors — checks that public money is spent lawfully. It also has to give prior clearance ("visto") to many large public contracts.

promptPt: Qual é o tribunal que está no topo da hierarquia dos tribunais judiciais?
options: O Tribunal da Relação de Lisboa
explanation: The Supreme Court of Justice heads the ordinary judicial courts, which handle civil and criminal cases. The Supreme Administrative Court heads a separate branch, for administrative and tax disputes.

promptPt: Qual é a função principal do Ministério Público?
options: Exercer a ação penal, ou seja, acusar em nome do Estado
explanation: The Ministério Público works alongside the courts and brings prosecutions; it does not judge. In Portugal it also defends the interests of children, absent persons and workers in certain proceedings.

promptPt: A quem podem os cidadãos apresentar queixas por ações ou omissões dos poderes públicos?
options: Ao Presidente da Assembleia da República
explanation: The Provedor de Justiça is Portugal's ombudsman: an independent office, its holder designated by Parliament, that receives complaints about the public authorities. The Ombudsman cannot overturn decisions but issues recommendations.
source: CRP, art. 23.º (texto confirmado em parlamento.pt e tribunalconstitucional.pt).

promptPt: Como se chama o titular nomeado pelo Presidente da República para representar a República em cada região autónoma?
explanation: Since the 2004 constitutional revision the post is called Representante da República, appointed by the President. The older title "Ministro da República" is precisely the trap answer here.

promptPt: Segundo a Constituição, quais são as categorias de autarquias locais?
options: Os distritos, os municípios e as freguesias
As regiões autónomas, os municípios e as freguesias
Apenas os municípios e as freguesias
As freguesias, os municípios e as regiões administrativas
explanation: Article 236 lists three: parishes, municipalities and administrative regions. Districts are not local authorities, and the autonomous regions belong to a different constitutional category altogether.

promptPt: Por que motivo não existem regiões administrativas em Portugal continental?
options: Porque, apesar de estarem previstas na Constituição, foram rejeitadas no referendo de 1998
Porque foram extintas pela reforma administrativa de 2013
Porque a Constituição as proíbe expressamente
Porque foram substituídas pelas comunidades intermunicipais em 1986
explanation: Administrative regions exist on paper in the Constitution but were never created: voters rejected them in the 1998 referendum. This is a favourite question because the answer is "they are foreseen but do not exist".

promptPt: Qual é o órgão executivo de um município?
options: A Câmara Municipal, presidida pelo Presidente da Câmara
explanation: Each municipality has an executive body, the Câmara Municipal led by the mayor, and a deliberative body, the Assembleia Municipal. The same executive/deliberative pairing repeats at parish level.

promptPt: Qual é o órgão executivo de uma freguesia?
explanation: The Junta de Freguesia is the parish executive; the Assembleia de Freguesia is its deliberative counterpart. The junta is where residents go for many everyday certificates and local services.

promptPt: De quantos em quantos anos se realizam as eleições autárquicas?
explanation: Local elections are held every four years; the most recent were on 12 October 2025. Note that EU citizens and some non-EU residents may vote in local elections under conditions of reciprocity, even though they cannot vote for President.
source: Comissão Nacional de Eleições — Eleições Autárquicas 2025; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §6.

promptPt: A que distrito pertence o município de Torres Vedras?
explanation: Torres Vedras is a municipality in the Lisbon district, on the Atlantic coast north of the capital. Santa Cruz is a coastal area within that same municipality.

promptPt: Em que data aderiu Portugal à Comunidade Económica Europeia, hoje União Europeia?
explanation: Portugal joined the EEC on 1 January 1986, on the same day as Spain. 12 June 1985 is the date the Accession Treaty was signed, at the Jerónimos Monastery in Lisbon — a classic distractor.
source: União Europeia — ficha de país, Portugal; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §7.

promptPt: Onde foi assinado o Tratado de Adesão de Portugal à Comunidade Económica Europeia, a 12 de junho de 1985?
options: No Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, em Lisboa
No Palácio de Belém, em Lisboa
No Palácio da Bolsa, no Porto
No Palácio de São Bento, em Lisboa
explanation: The Accession Treaty was signed at the Jerónimos Monastery in Belém, a site chosen for its symbolic weight. The same monastery holds the tombs of Camões and Vasco da Gama.

promptPt: Em que ano entrou Portugal no espaço Schengen?
explanation: Portugal joined the Schengen area on 26 March 1995, which is why there are no routine border checks with Spain. Do not confuse it with 1986 (EEC accession) or 2002 (euro notes and coins).
source: União Europeia — ficha de país, Portugal; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §7.

promptPt: Em que ano começaram a circular as notas e moedas de euro em Portugal?
explanation: Portugal adopted the euro as its currency on 1 January 1999, but notes and coins only entered circulation in 2002. Both dates are correct for different things — read the question carefully.
source: União Europeia — ficha de país, Portugal; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §7.

promptPt: Quantos deputados elege Portugal para o Parlamento Europeu?
explanation: Portugal elects 21 members of the European Parliament. Careful with 18 and 27, which are the number of mainland districts and the number of EU Member States.
source: União Europeia — ficha de país, Portugal; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §7.

promptPt: Qual é a relação de Portugal com a NATO?
options: Portugal aderiu à NATO apenas em 1986, com a entrada na CEE
Portugal é membro fundador, tendo assinado o Tratado do Atlântico Norte em 1949
Portugal nunca fez parte da NATO
Portugal aderiu à NATO depois da Revolução de 25 de abril de 1974
explanation: Portugal is a founding member of NATO, having signed the North Atlantic Treaty in Washington on 4 April 1949 — during the dictatorship, which surprises many learners. NATO today has 32 members.

promptPt: Desde que ano é Portugal membro da Organização das Nações Unidas?
explanation: Portugal joined the UN in 1955, ten years after the organisation was founded in 1945. 1949 is NATO, not the UN.

promptPt: Em que ano e em que cidade foi criada a CPLP — Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa?
explanation: The CPLP was created on 17 July 1996 in Lisbon, with seven founding states. Timor-Leste joined in 2002 after independence, bringing a later expansion.

promptPt: Qual destes países NÃO é Estado-membro da CPLP?
explanation: The CPLP brings together countries where Portuguese is an official language; Spain is not one of them. Timor-Leste, Cape Verde and São Tomé e Príncipe are all members.

promptPt: Segundo o artigo 11.º da Constituição, quais são os símbolos nacionais e a língua oficial da República?
options: A Bandeira Nacional, o Hino Nacional e a língua portuguesa
A Bandeira Nacional, o brasão de armas e o Dia de Portugal
O Hino Nacional, a esfera armilar e a língua portuguesa
A Bandeira Nacional, o Hino Nacional e o Palácio de Belém
explanation: Article 11 fixes three things: the national flag, the national anthem and Portuguese as the official language. Notice that the language itself is constitutionally protected — which is part of why the citizenship law can require knowledge of it.

promptPt: Como estão dispostas as cores da Bandeira Nacional?
options: Vermelho do lado da haste e verde do lado de fora
Verde-escuro do lado da haste e vermelho do lado de fora
Duas faixas horizontais, verde em cima e vermelha em baixo
Verde ao centro, com duas faixas vermelhas nos lados
explanation: The flag is divided vertically, with dark green at the hoist (the side attached to the pole) and scarlet at the fly. Getting the order the wrong way round is the most common mistake.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: Que proporção do comprimento da bandeira ocupa cada cor?
options: Dois quintos verde e três quintos vermelho
Um terço verde e dois terços vermelho
Três quintos verde e dois quintos vermelho
explanation: Green takes two fifths of the length and red takes three fifths, so the red field is the larger of the two. The armillary sphere and shield sit over the join between them.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: O que representa a esfera armilar na Bandeira Nacional?
options: A navegação e os Descobrimentos, evocando o reinado de D. Manuel I
A religião católica e as ordens militares
A monarquia e a Casa de Bragança
A união entre Portugal e as regiões autónomas
explanation: The armillary sphere is a navigational instrument and was the personal emblem of King Manuel I. On the flag it stands for the Age of Discovery and Portugal's maritime history.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: Quantos castelos amarelos tem a bordadura vermelha do escudo das Armas Nacionais?
explanation: There are seven yellow castles on the red border of the shield. Five is the number of blue shields (the "quinas") inside it — the two numbers are easy to swap by mistake.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: Como se chamam os cinco escudetes azuis dispostos em cruz no escudo branco?
explanation: The five small blue shields arranged in a cross are called "as quinas", and they recall the founding of the nation. The "besantes" are the small white discs inside each of them.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: Quantos besantes tem cada um dos cinco escudetes azuis?
explanation: Each of the five blue shields carries five bezants, small white roundels. So the shield gives you three fives to remember: five quinas, five bezants each, plus seven castles on the border.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: Em que ano foi aprovada a Bandeira Nacional atualmente em uso?
explanation: The current flag was approved by decree of the Constituent National Assembly on 19 June 1911, shortly after the Republic was proclaimed on 5 October 1910. A second decree, of 30 June 1911, fixed its dimensions and details.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: De onde vêm as cores verde e vermelha da bandeira?
options: Das cores da bandeira do Reino de Portugal
Do movimento republicano, usadas na revolução de 5 de outubro de 1910
Das cores da bandeira da Ordem de Cristo
Das cores adotadas pela Constituição de 1976
explanation: Green and red were the colours of the republican movement, seen in the failed revolt of 31 January 1891 and then in the successful revolution of 5 October 1910. The monarchy's flag had been blue and white.
source: Presidência da República — Bandeira Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.1.

promptPt: Como se chama o Hino Nacional de Portugal?
explanation: The national anthem is "A Portuguesa". "Grândola, Vila Morena" is the song used as a signal during the 1974 revolution and is much loved, but it is not the anthem.
source: Presidência da República — Hino Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.2.

promptPt: Quem escreveu a letra de "A Portuguesa"?
explanation: The lyrics are by Henrique Lopes de Mendonça and the music by Alfredo Keil. Examiners like to swap the two names round, so learn which one did which.
source: Presidência da República — Hino Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.2.

promptPt: Quem compôs a música de "A Portuguesa"?
explanation: Alfredo Keil wrote the music in 1890. He was a composer and painter of German descent, born in Lisbon.
source: Presidência da República — Hino Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.2.

promptPt: Em que contexto histórico foi composta "A Portuguesa", em 1890?
options: Na sequência da Revolução dos Cravos
Na sequência do terramoto de Lisboa
Na sequência da adesão de Portugal à CEE
explanation: It was written in 1890 as a patriotic protest after the British Ultimatum, which forced Portugal to give up its claim to the territory between Angola and Mozambique. It then became the march of the republican revolt of 31 January 1891.
source: Presidência da República — Hino Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.2.

promptPt: Como começa a primeira estrofe do Hino Nacional?
explanation: The first verse opens "Heróis do mar, nobre povo, / Nação valente, imortal". "Às armas, às armas!" is the beginning of the chorus, not of the verse.
source: Presidência da República — Hino Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.2.

promptPt: O que se canta habitualmente nas cerimónias oficiais?
options: As três estrofes e o refrão
Apenas a primeira estrofe e o refrão
explanation: At official ceremonies only the first verse and the chorus are sung, even though the anthem has three verses. If you attend a citizenship ceremony or a football match, that is the version you will hear.
source: Presidência da República — Hino Nacional; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.2.

promptPt: Qual é o nome completo do feriado que se celebra a 10 de junho?
options: Dia de Portugal, de Camões e das Comunidades Portuguesas
explanation: The full official name has three parts: Portugal, Camões and the Portuguese communities abroad. The emigrant communities were added to the name because 10 June is celebrated in the diaspora as well.
source: Presidência da República — Dia de Portugal; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.3.

promptPt: Porque se escolheu o dia 10 de junho para o Dia de Portugal?
options: Porque foi o dia da fundação do reino, em 1143
Porque foi o dia da morte de Luís Vaz de Camões, em 1580
Porque foi o dia da assinatura do Tratado de Alcanizes
Porque foi o dia da implantação da República
explanation: 10 June marks the death of Camões, author of Os Lusíadas, in 1580. Portugal is unusual in having its national day tied to a poet rather than to a battle or a declaration of independence.
source: Presidência da República — Dia de Portugal; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.3 e §10.1.

promptPt: Quem organiza anualmente as comemorações do Dia de Portugal?
options: O Presidente da República, em articulação com o Governo
explanation: The President organises the commemorations jointly with the Government, and chooses a different host location each year. In 2026 they took place on Terceira island, in the Azores, and in Luxembourg.
source: Presidência da República — Dia de Portugal; Decreto-Lei n.º 20-A/2016; dossiê `estado-cultura.md` §5.3.

promptPt: Que parte da Constituição trata dos direitos e deveres fundamentais?
explanation: Part I of the Constitution is devoted to fundamental rights and duties, and it comes before the parts on the economy and on the organisation of political power. That ordering is deliberate: rights come first.

promptPt: O que estabelece o princípio da igualdade, no artigo 13.º da Constituição?
options: Que todos os cidadãos têm o mesmo rendimento
Que todos os cidadãos têm a mesma dignidade social e são iguais perante a lei
Que os estrangeiros não podem ser tratados como os portugueses
Que apenas os cidadãos portugueses são iguais perante a lei
explanation: Article 13 guarantees equal social dignity and equality before the law. It is about equal treatment by the law, not about everyone having the same income.

promptPt: Segundo o artigo 13.º, ninguém pode ser prejudicado ou privilegiado em razão de...
options: apenas do sexo e da idade
apenas da religião e das convicções políticas
apenas da situação económica e da condição social
ascendência, sexo, raça, língua, território de origem, religião, convicções políticas, instrução, situação económica, condição social ou orientação sexual
explanation: The Constitution gives a long, explicit list of prohibited grounds of discrimination, and sexual orientation was added to it in the 2004 revision. If a question offers a short list, it is almost certainly the wrong answer.

promptPt: Qual é a situação da pena de morte em Portugal?
options: Está prevista apenas para crimes cometidos em tempo de guerra
Foi abolida pela Constituição de 1976 e pode ser reposta por referendo
Está abolida em todas as circunstâncias
explanation: Article 24 declares human life inviolable and abolishes the death penalty in all circumstances, with no wartime exception. Portugal abolished it for civil crimes as early as 1867, among the first countries in Europe.

promptPt: Em que ano aboliu Portugal a pena de morte para crimes civis?
explanation: Portugal abolished the death penalty for civil crimes in 1867, long before the Republic and long before the current Constitution. It is a point of national pride and appears often in civics material.

promptPt: Qual é a relação entre o Estado português e a religião?
options: O catolicismo é a religião oficial do Estado
O Estado proíbe a prática religiosa em público
Só as religiões reconhecidas por lei podem ter culto
O Estado é laico e não professa nenhuma religião; a liberdade de consciência, de religião e de culto é inviolável
explanation: Article 41 makes freedom of conscience, religion and worship inviolable, and the State professes no religion. Most Portuguese people are culturally Roman Catholic, but that is a social fact, not a legal status.

promptPt: Qual destes direitos NÃO está garantido pela Constituição portuguesa?
options: A liberdade de expressão e de informação
O direito de reunião e de manifestação
O direito de porte de arma para defesa pessoal
explanation: Freedom of expression, assembly, demonstration, association and the right to strike are all constitutionally guaranteed. There is no constitutional right to bear arms in Portugal; firearms are tightly regulated by ordinary law.

promptPt: Como garante a Constituição o direito à proteção da saúde?
options: Através de seguros de saúde privados obrigatórios
Através de um Serviço Nacional de Saúde universal e tendencialmente gratuito
Apenas para os cidadãos portugueses de origem
Apenas para quem tenha descontado para a Segurança Social
explanation: The Constitution guarantees health protection through a universal National Health Service that is "tendencialmente gratuito" — free at the point of use, apart from moderating fees. Legal residents have access to it, not only Portuguese nationals.

promptPt: O que diz a Constituição sobre o ensino básico?
options: É obrigatório apenas para cidadãos portugueses
É gratuito apenas nas escolas privadas com contrato
explanation: Basic schooling is universal, compulsory and free. The Constitution also guarantees freedom to learn and to teach, in article 43.

promptPt: Segundo o artigo 15.º da Constituição, que direitos têm os estrangeiros e apátridas que residem em Portugal?
options: Nenhuns, até obterem a nacionalidade portuguesa
Apenas o direito à saúde e à educação
Apenas os direitos previstos no seu título de residência
Em regra, os mesmos direitos e deveres dos cidadãos portugueses
explanation: Article 15 puts resident foreigners and stateless people on the same footing as Portuguese citizens as a general rule. This is one of the most important articles for immigrants to know, and it works both ways: the same duties apply too.

promptPt: Quais são as principais exceções à igualdade de direitos entre estrangeiros residentes e cidadãos portugueses?
options: O direito à saúde e à educação
O direito ao trabalho e à propriedade
Os direitos políticos e o exercício de funções públicas de soberania
O direito de acesso aos tribunais
explanation: The exceptions concern mainly political rights, sovereign public office, and rights the law reserves to nationals. Health, education, work, property and access to the courts are not among them.

promptPt: A partir de que idade se adquire o direito de voto em Portugal?
explanation: Article 49 gives the right to vote to all citizens over eighteen, save for incapacities laid down by general law. Compare this with the minimum age of 35 for standing as President.
source: CRP, art. 49.º (texto confirmado em parlamento.pt e tribunalconstitucional.pt).

promptPt: O voto é obrigatório em Portugal?
options: Sim, e quem não votar paga uma coima
Sim, mas apenas nas eleições legislativas
Não — votar é um dever cívico, mas o voto não é obrigatório
explanation: Voting is described as a civic duty but it is not legally compulsory, and there is no penalty for abstaining. Some countries in the region do impose compulsory voting, so do not assume.

promptPt: Quais são deveres fundamentais de quem vive em Portugal?
options: Votar em todas as eleições e pertencer a um partido
Cumprir a Constituição e as leis, pagar impostos, defender o país, respeitar os direitos dos outros e proteger o ambiente e o património
explanation: Rights come with duties, and the Constitution lists several: obeying the law, paying taxes, defending the country, respecting other people's rights and protecting the environment and heritage. Joining a party is a freedom, never a duty.

promptPt: Em que circunstâncias podem ser suspensos os direitos, liberdades e garantias?
options: Sempre que o Governo o entender necessário
Apenas em estado de sítio ou estado de emergência, declarados na forma prevista na Constituição
explanation: Article 19 allows suspension only under a declared state of siege or state of emergency, following the constitutional procedure. Portugal used a state of emergency during the COVID-19 pandemic, which is the most recent real example.
source: CRP, art. 19.º (texto confirmado em parlamento.pt e tribunalconstitucional.pt).

promptPt: O que é o direito de resistência, previsto no artigo 21.º da Constituição?
options: O direito de resistir a qualquer ordem que ofenda os seus direitos, liberdades e garantias e de repelir pela força qualquer agressão, quando não seja possível recorrer à autoridade pública
O direito de recusar pagar impostos por desacordo político
O direito de fazer greve em qualquer profissão
O direito de não cumprir sentenças judiciais desfavoráveis
explanation: The right of resistance allows you to refuse an order that violates your fundamental rights, and to repel force with force when the public authorities cannot be reached in time. It is a narrow, last-resort right, not a general licence to disobey the law.
source: CRP, art. 21.º (texto confirmado em parlamento.pt e tribunalconstitucional.pt).

promptPt: Para que serve o habeas corpus, previsto no artigo 31.º da Constituição?
options: Para pedir a revisão de uma sentença já transitada em julgado
Para reclamar de uma decisão da Segurança Social
Para reagir contra prisão ou detenção ilegal, mediante requerimento ao tribunal competente
Para pedir asilo político em Portugal
explanation: Habeas corpus is the remedy against abuse of power through unlawful arrest or detention, brought before the competent court. It is one of the oldest guarantees of individual liberty and exists in many legal systems.
source: CRP, art. 31.º (texto confirmado em parlamento.pt e tribunalconstitucional.pt).

promptPt: Que declaração exige a Lei da Nacionalidade a quem pede a naturalização portuguesa?
options: Uma declaração de renúncia à nacionalidade de origem
Uma declaração solene de adesão aos princípios fundamentais do Estado de direito democrático
Uma declaração de filiação num partido político português
explanation: The alínea e) of article 6(1) requires applicants to declare solemnly their adherence to the fundamental principles of the democratic rule of law. Note that this is a declaration, not a test — and Portugal does not require you to give up your original nationality.
source: Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, de 18 de maio, art. 6.º n.º 1 al. e); dossiê `regulamento.md` §3.

promptPt: Segundo o n.º 10 do artigo 6.º da Lei da Nacionalidade, de que estão presumivelmente dispensados os nacionais de países de língua oficial portuguesa?
options: De todos os requisitos de conhecimento
Apenas da primeira parte da alínea c), ou seja, do conhecimento da língua portuguesa
Da declaração solene de adesão aos princípios do Estado de direito democrático
explanation: The presumption is expressly limited to the *first part* of alínea c) — the language. Culture, history, national symbols and the civics requirements of alínea d) are not covered, so CPLP nationals still have to show that knowledge. The presumption can also be rebutted where a lack of Portuguese is manifest.
source: Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, art. 6.º n.º 10 (texto integral lido em files.diariodarepublica.pt); dossiê `regulamento.md` §4.

promptPt: Que lei se aplica aos pedidos de nacionalidade que já estavam pendentes a 19 de maio de 2026?
options: A nova lei, incluindo os novos requisitos de conhecimento
Uma lei mista, escolhida pelo requerente
A Lei n.º 37/81 na redação anterior, ou seja, a lei antiga
Nenhuma — os pedidos pendentes foram anulados
explanation: Article 7(2) of Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026 keeps pending applications under the old law, with the old residence periods and no knowledge test. If you filed before 19 May 2026, check your submission date carefully before paying for exam preparation.
source: Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, art. 7.º n.º 2; dossiê `regulamento.md` §6.

promptPt: Quais são as matérias que a lei fixa como conteúdo do requisito de conhecimento para a naturalização?
options: Apenas os direitos e deveres fundamentais
A língua e a cultura portuguesas, a história, os símbolos nacionais, os direitos e deveres fundamentais e a organização política do Estado português
explanation: The alíneas c) and d) of article 6(1) together set five domains: language, culture, history, national symbols, and fundamental rights and duties plus the political organisation of the State. That is the syllabus fixed by statute — the exam format itself has not yet been regulated.
source: Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, art. 6.º n.º 1 als. c) e d); dossiê `regulamento.md` §3.

promptPt: Que órgão da Constituição garante que os cidadãos podem queixar-se da Administração Pública sem recorrer aos tribunais?
explanation: The Ombudsman offers a free, non-judicial route for complaints against the public authorities, and its holder is designated by Parliament. Using it does not stop you from going to court as well.
source: CRP, art. 23.º (texto confirmado em parlamento.pt e tribunalconstitucional.pt).

promptPt: Em que ano se deu a Batalha de São Mamede?
explanation: In 1128 Afonso Henriques won at São Mamede and took control of the county of Portucale. This battle is the traditional starting point of Portugal as a separate country. Do not confuse it with 1143, the year he began to use the title of king.

promptPt: Perto de que cidade se deu a Batalha de São Mamede?
explanation: São Mamede was fought near Guimarães, in the north of the country. For this reason Guimarães is often called "o berço da nação" — the cradle of the nation. The castle there is one of Portugal's best-known monuments.

promptPt: Quem venceu a Batalha de São Mamede, em 1128?
explanation: Afonso Henriques is the first king of Portugal and the name every citizenship test expects here. The other three kings all come much later. Remember the pair: Afonso Henriques and 1128.

promptPt: Em que ano venceu D. Afonso Henriques a Batalha de Ourique, contra os mouros?
explanation: Ourique was fought in 1139 against the Moors. The three early dates run in a short sequence: 1128 São Mamede, 1139 Ourique, 1147 the conquest of Lisbon. Learning them as a chain is easier than learning them one by one.

promptPt: O que aconteceu em 1143, no encontro de Zamora com Afonso VII de Leão e Castela?
options: O papa reconheceu Portugal como reino
D. Afonso Henriques passou a usar o título de rei
explanation: At the meeting of Zamora, on 5 October 1143, Afonso Henriques began to use the title of king. This is the answer a test expects for "when was Portugal born?". The papal recognition is a different event, in 1179.

promptPt: Qual foi o documento de 1179 que reconheceu Portugal como reino independente?
explanation: In 1179 the Pope issued the bull *Manifestis Probatum*, which recognised Portugal as an independent kingdom. This was the legal recognition; 1143 was only the title. Know both dates and what each one means.

promptPt: Que papa emitiu a bula Manifestis Probatum?
explanation: Pope Alexander III issued the bull in 1179. At the time, recognition by the Pope was what made a new kingdom legitimate in the eyes of the rest of Europe. Link the three words together: 1179, Alexandre III, *Manifestis Probatum*.

promptPt: Em que ano é que D. Afonso Henriques conquistou Lisboa aos mouros?
explanation: Lisbon was taken in 1147, with help from crusaders sailing from northern Europe to the Holy Land. Lisbon only became the capital later; at this point the centre of the kingdom was still in the north.

promptPt: Quem ajudou D. Afonso Henriques a conquistar Lisboa em 1147?
options: Cruzados vindos do norte da Europa
explanation: Crusader fleets from northern Europe stopped in Portugal on their way to the Holy Land and joined the siege of Lisbon. This kind of foreign help was common in the Reconquest. Note the trap: Brazil was only reached in 1500, more than three centuries later.

promptPt: Que rei conquistou o Algarve em 1249?
explanation: Afonso III took the Algarve in 1249, which completed the Reconquest and fixed Portugal's territory in the south. From that year the country had roughly the shape you see on the map today.

promptPt: O que terminou em Portugal com a conquista do Algarve, em 1249?
explanation: The Reconquest — the long process of taking the territory from Moorish rule — ended in 1249. Portugal finished it earlier than its neighbours in the peninsula. The other three events belong to much later centuries.

promptPt: O que fixou o Tratado de Alcanizes, de 1297?
options: As fronteiras entre Portugal e Castela
A divisão do mundo com Castela
A entrada de Portugal na Europa
explanation: The Treaty of Alcanizes, in 1297, set the border between Portugal and Castile. That is why Portugal has one of the oldest borders in Europe — over seven hundred years old and almost unchanged. Do not mix it up with Tordesillas (1494), which divided lands overseas.

promptPt: Que batalha, em 1385, garantiu a independência de Portugal face a Castela?
explanation: Aljubarrota, in 1385, stopped the Castilian claim to the Portuguese throne and kept the country independent. It is one of the most famous battles in Portuguese history. Alcácer-Quibir (1578) and Alcântara (1580) are later defeats — do not confuse them.

promptPt: Que dinastia começou com D. João I, Mestre de Avis, depois de 1385?
explanation: John I, Master of the Order of Avis, became king and started the second dynasty, the House of Avis. This is the dynasty of the Discoveries. Braganza comes only in 1640, after the Spanish period.

promptPt: Que conquista, em 1415, marca o começo da expansão portuguesa?
explanation: In 1415 the forces of John I took Ceuta, in North Africa. Tests treat this as the starting date of the Portuguese overseas expansion. Goa and Brazil came later, once the sea routes were open.

promptPt: Onde fica Ceuta, conquistada em 1415?
explanation: Ceuta is on the North African coast, just across from the Strait of Gibraltar. Taking it gave Portugal a foothold outside Europe for the first time. Today Ceuta is Spanish territory.

promptPt: O que dividiu o Tratado de Tordesilhas, de 1494?
options: O mundo por descobrir entre Portugal e Castela
O território de Portugal entre dois reis
As colónias africanas entre Portugal e França
O Algarve entre cristãos e mouros
explanation: The Treaty of Tordesillas, in 1494, split the yet-undiscovered world between Portugal and Castile along a meridian in the Atlantic. It is the reason Brazil later became Portuguese and the rest of South America Spanish. The line was drawn before anyone knew what was actually there.

promptPt: Quem chegou à Índia por via marítima, em 1498?
explanation: Vasco da Gama reached Calicut, in India, in 1498, opening the sea route around Africa. It was the commercial goal behind decades of Portuguese voyages. Cabral is the name for Brazil, two years later.

promptPt: A que cidade da Índia chegou Vasco da Gama em 1498?
explanation: He landed at Calicut (Calecute in Portuguese), on the south-west coast of India. Goa, Daman and Diu became Portuguese territories later and stayed Portuguese until 1961. Keep 1498 and Calecute together.

promptPt: Quem chegou ao Brasil em 1500?
explanation: Pedro Álvares Cabral reached Brazil in 1500, while sailing towards India. Brazil then stayed linked to Portugal until it declared independence in 1822. The pair to memorise is Cabral–1500–Brasil.

promptPt: O que fez o Tratado de Saragoça, de 1529?
options: Prolongou a linha de Tordesilhas para o outro hemisfério
explanation: The Treaty of Zaragoza, of 22 April 1529, extended the Tordesillas line into the other half of the globe and settled the dispute over the Moluccas. Portugal paid Charles V 350,000 gold ducats. Think of it as "Tordesillas, part two".

promptPt: O que aconteceu a 4 de agosto de 1578, na Batalha de Alcácer-Quibir?
options: O rei D. Sebastião morreu, sem deixar herdeiros
explanation: King Sebastian died at Alcácer-Quibir, in Morocco, leaving no heir. The succession crisis that followed put Portugal under Spanish kings two years later. This defeat is the hinge between the age of expansion and the loss of independence.

promptPt: O que é o sebastianismo?
options: Uma corrente de arquitetura do século XVIII
Um partido político da Primeira República
Um imposto criado pelo Marquês de Pombal
A crença de que D. Sebastião havia de voltar para salvar o país
explanation: After 1578 many people refused to accept that the king was dead and believed he would return one misty morning to save the country. This belief is called *sebastianismo*, and it is still a living cultural reference in books and everyday speech. If someone says a plan is "sebastianista", they mean it is wishful thinking.

promptPt: O que caracterizou o período entre 1580 e 1640 em Portugal?
options: Portugal não teve rei nem governo
explanation: Between 1580 and 1640 the kings of Spain were also kings of Portugal. This period is called the *período filipino* or the Iberian Union. Portugal kept its own laws and institutions, but lost control of its foreign policy.

promptPt: Quem foi derrotado na Batalha de Alcântara, em agosto de 1580?
explanation: António, Prior of Crato, was the Portuguese candidate to the throne and was defeated at Alcântara in 1580. After that, Philip II of Spain became Philip I of Portugal, accepted at the Cortes of Tomar in 1581. This is how the Iberian Union began.

promptPt: O que aconteceu a 1 de dezembro de 1640?
options: A adesão à Comunidade Económica Europeia
explanation: On 1 December 1640 a group of noblemen overthrew Spanish rule and Portugal recovered its independence. This is the *Restauração da Independência*. It is still a national public holiday.

promptPt: Que dinastia começou com D. João IV, aclamado rei a 15 de dezembro de 1640?
explanation: The Duke of Braganza was acclaimed King John IV and began the fourth dynasty, the House of Braganza. It ruled until the end of the monarchy in 1910. Avis is the dynasty of the Discoveries, two centuries earlier.

promptPt: Quanto tempo durou a Guerra da Restauração?
explanation: The Restoration War lasted 28 years, from 1640 to 1668. Recovering the crown in 1640 was quick; getting Spain to accept it took nearly three decades. Careful with the number 48 — that is the length of the Estado Novo, a different fact.

promptPt: O que ficou decidido no Tratado de Lisboa, de 13 de fevereiro de 1668?
options: Espanha reconheceu a independência de Portugal
Portugal e Castela dividiram o Atlântico
