explanation: With the Treaty of Lisbon of 1668, Spain finally recognised Portuguese independence and the Restoration War ended. Note there is a modern European treaty with the same name, signed in Lisbon in 2007 — in a history question, 1668 is the one that matters.

promptPt: O que se comemora no feriado nacional de 1 de dezembro?
explanation: 1 December marks the Restoration of Independence of 1640. Keep the four big civic dates apart: 25 April is Liberty Day, 10 June is Portugal Day, 5 October is the Republic, 1 December is the Restoration.

promptPt: Em que data se deu o grande terramoto de Lisboa?
explanation: The earthquake struck on the morning of 1 November 1755, at about half past nine. It is one of the most important events in Portuguese history and shaped the city you walk through today. Remember the date as "All Saints' Day, 1755".

promptPt: Que dia religioso se celebrava quando o terramoto atingiu Lisboa?
options: O Dia de Todos os Santos
explanation: It was All Saints' Day, so the churches were full of people at Mass. That is one reason the number of victims was so high and the shock so deep. The date is still a public holiday in Portugal.

promptPt: O que se seguiu ao terramoto de 1755 e aumentou a destruição de Lisboa?
explanation: After the shaking came a tsunami along the river and fires that burned for days. Tens of thousands of people died and about 85% of Lisbon's buildings were destroyed. The three-part sequence — quake, wave, fire — is a classic test detail.

promptPt: Quem era o rei de Portugal na altura do terramoto de 1755?
explanation: The king was Joseph I. He survived because the royal family was outside Lisbon that morning, and afterwards he refused to live in a stone palace again. His minister took charge of the rebuilding.

promptPt: Quem dirigiu a reconstrução de Lisboa depois do terramoto?
explanation: The Marquis of Pombal, minister of Joseph I, organised the emergency response and the rebuilding of the city centre. The rebuilt district is called the *Baixa Pombalina* and carries his name to this day.

promptPt: O que é a «gaiola pombalina»?
options: Um imposto sobre o comércio com o Brasil
Uma estrutura de madeira feita para resistir aos sismos
Um estilo de pintura do século XVIII
explanation: The *gaiola pombalina* is a wooden cage-like frame built inside the walls of the new Baixa buildings so they could flex in an earthquake. It is one of the earliest earthquake-resistant building systems in the world. The word *gaiola* literally means "cage".

promptPt: Porque é que o inquérito do Marquês de Pombal às paróquias é famoso?
options: Está na origem da sismologia moderna
Serviu para criar o primeiro censo do império
explanation: Pombal sent parishes across the country a questionnaire asking what exactly they had felt and seen. Collecting systematic data about an earthquake had never been done before, and historians treat it as the beginning of modern seismology. It is a good example of the Enlightenment reaching Portugal.

promptPt: Quantas invasões francesas sofreu Portugal entre 1807 e 1811?
explanation: There were three French invasions between 1807 and 1811, during the Napoleonic Wars. Portugal was attacked because it refused to close its ports to British trade. British and Portuguese forces fought together against them.

promptPt: Para onde partiu a família real portuguesa em 1807?
explanation: In 1807, as the French approached, the royal family sailed to Brazil and Rio de Janeiro became the capital of the empire. It is the only case in history of a European court moving to a colony. Brazil declared independence fifteen years later, in 1822.

promptPt: Qual era o objetivo das Linhas de Torres Vedras?
options: Ligar Lisboa ao Porto por caminho de ferro
explanation: The Lines of Torres Vedras were a defensive system of forts built north of Lisbon to stop the French army from reaching the capital. They worked: the French never got through. If you live near Torres Vedras, this history happened on your doorstep.

promptPt: Quem mandou construir as Linhas de Torres Vedras, a partir de outubro de 1809?
explanation: Wellington, the British commander, ordered the Lines built from October 1809. Masséna is the opposite side of the story — the French marshal who could not get past them. Keep the two names straight.

promptPt: De quantas fortificações era feito o sistema das Linhas de Torres Vedras?
explanation: The system had 152 fortifications built across the hills between the sea and the Tagus. Several of them have been restored and can be visited today along the *Rota Histórica das Linhas de Torres*. The number 152 is the one to remember.

promptPt: O que fez o exército francês do marechal Masséna diante das Linhas de Torres Vedras?
options: Passou as Linhas e tomou Lisboa
Não conseguiu passar e retirou-se em fevereiro de 1811
explanation: Masséna arrived in October 1810, found the Lines impassable, waited through the winter and withdrew in February 1811. The French never took Lisbon. This retreat effectively ended the third invasion.

promptPt: Em que ano declarou o Brasil a independência?
explanation: Brazil declared independence in 1822, after the court had returned to Lisbon. The same year, Portugal approved its first Constitution — two big 1822 facts worth linking together. Portugal and Brazil have kept close ties ever since, which is why Brazilians appear in the nationality law today.

promptPt: Em que cidade começou a Revolução Liberal, a 24 de agosto de 1820?
explanation: The Liberal Revolution began in Porto on 24 August 1820 and spread from there. Its goal was a constitution and an elected parliament instead of absolute royal power. Porto has a long tradition of starting political movements in Portugal.

promptPt: Em que ano foi aprovada a primeira Constituição portuguesa?
explanation: The first Portuguese Constitution was approved on 23 September 1822, after the Constituent Cortes first met in January 1821. It limited the king's power for the first time. The 1826 date belongs to a different document, the Constitutional Charter.

promptPt: Quem outorgou a Carta Constitucional de 1826?
explanation: Peter IV granted the Constitutional Charter in 1826. It created two chambers and a limited vote based on property, so it was less democratic than the 1822 Constitution. The fight between the Charter and the 1822 text is at the root of the civil war that followed.

promptPt: Quem se enfrentou na guerra civil portuguesa de 1828 a 1834?
options: Liberais e absolutistas, entre D. Pedro e D. Miguel
explanation: The civil war of 1828–1834 set the liberals, behind Peter, against the absolutists, behind Miguel. The liberals won in 1834, and constitutional monarchy became the settled system. Republicans only become a serious force much later, at the end of the century.

promptPt: Que rainha jurou uma nova Constituição a 4 de abril de 1838?
explanation: Queen Maria II swore the new Constitution of 1838, after the liberal victory of 1834. She is the queen most associated with the consolidation of the constitutional monarchy. Lisbon's national theatre carries her name.

promptPt: Qual foi a consequência política do Ultimato britânico de 1890?
options: Portugal entrou na Primeira Guerra Mundial
O rei renunciou ao trono nesse mesmo ano
Provocou uma grave crise e reforçou o movimento republicano
explanation: In 1890 Britain demanded that Portugal withdraw from territory between Angola and Mozambique, and the government gave in. The humiliation caused a serious political crisis and pushed many people towards the republican movement. Twenty years later the monarchy fell.

promptPt: O que aconteceu a 1 de fevereiro de 1908, em Lisboa?
options: O rei D. Carlos e o príncipe herdeiro foram assassinados
explanation: On 1 February 1908 King Carlos and the crown prince were shot dead in Lisbon — the event known as the *Regicídio*. His younger son became Manuel II, the last king of Portugal. The monarchy survived only two more years.

promptPt: Em que data foi implantada a República em Portugal?
explanation: The Republic was proclaimed on 5 October 1910, ending the monarchy. The date is still a national public holiday. Do not confuse it with 25 April, which is 1974 and a different revolution altogether.

promptPt: Quem proclamou a República, da varanda da Câmara Municipal de Lisboa?
explanation: José Relvas read out the proclamation from the balcony of Lisbon City Hall on 5 October 1910. Teófilo Braga then headed the Provisional Government and Manuel de Arriaga was the first elected President, in 1911. Three names, three different roles — keep them apart.

promptPt: Quem foi o último rei de Portugal?
explanation: Manuel II was the last king. He went into exile in 1910 and never returned to live in Portugal. He sailed from Ericeira, on the coast just south of Santa Cruz — a local connection worth remembering.

promptPt: Quem foi o primeiro Presidente da República eleito, em 1911?
explanation: Manuel de Arriaga was elected the first President of the Portuguese Republic in 1911, after Teófilo Braga had led the Provisional Government. Óscar Carmona belongs to the dictatorship, from 1926 onwards. The First Republic went through presidents very quickly and was politically unstable.

promptPt: Que símbolos nacionais adotou a República em 1910?
options: A bandeira azul e branca e o hino «Grândola, Vila Morena»
A bandeira verde e vermelha e o hino «A Portuguesa»
A bandeira verde e vermelha e o hino «Hino da Carta»
A bandeira azul e branca e o hino «A Portuguesa»
explanation: The Republic replaced the blue-and-white monarchical flag with the green-and-red flag still used today, and adopted "A Portuguesa" as the national anthem. "Grândola, Vila Morena" is a 1974 song, not the anthem. Symbols are explicitly named in the nationality law, so learn them well.

promptPt: O que se comemora no feriado nacional de 5 de outubro?
explanation: 5 October marks the proclamation of the Republic in 1910. Together with 1 December, 25 April and 10 June, it is one of the four civic national holidays. Tests like asking what each date celebrates.

promptPt: O que aconteceu a 28 de maio de 1926?
options: Portugal aderiu à Comunidade Económica Europeia
Um golpe militar pôs fim à Primeira República
explanation: On 28 May 1926 a military coup that started in Braga, led by General Gomes da Costa, ended the First Republic. It opened a military dictatorship that became the Estado Novo. Salazar only reached the top job later, in 1932.

promptPt: Quem foi Presidente da República entre 1926 e 1951?
explanation: Óscar Carmona took power in July 1926 and remained President until 1951. Under the Estado Novo the President had little real power; the head of government was the strong figure. That head of government was Salazar.

promptPt: Que cargo ocupou António de Oliveira Salazar em 1928?
explanation: Salazar entered the government as Finance Minister in 1928, with a reputation as an economics professor who could balance the budget. That role made him powerful enough to become head of government in 1932. He was never President of the Republic.

promptPt: A partir de que ano foi Salazar Presidente do Conselho de Ministros?
explanation: Salazar became Prime Minister (*Presidente do Conselho de Ministros*) in 1932 and stayed until 1968. The 1933 Constitution came the following year and gave the regime its formal shape. The order is: 1926 coup, 1928 Finance, 1932 head of government, 1933 Constitution.

promptPt: Que regime criou a Constituição de 1933?
explanation: The 1933 Constitution created the Estado Novo, an authoritarian and corporatist regime. It lasted until 1974 — about 48 years counting from the 1926 coup. It was one of the longest dictatorships in twentieth-century Europe.

promptPt: Qual destas afirmações sobre o Estado Novo é verdadeira?
options: Havia eleições livres com vários partidos
A Assembleia Nacional podia derrubar o Governo
A imprensa podia criticar o Governo sem limites
Havia censura, partido único e uma polícia política, a PIDE
explanation: The regime had censorship, a single legal party, a National Assembly with no real power and a political police force, the PIDE. Understanding what was absent — free elections, free press, free unions — is the point of this topic. It explains why 25 April 1974 matters so much to Portuguese people.

promptPt: Quem substituiu Salazar na chefia do Governo, em 1968?
explanation: Marcelo Caetano replaced Salazar in 1968, after Salazar became ill. He promised reform but kept the essential structure of the regime and the colonial war. He was the man in power when the revolution came in 1974.

promptPt: Em que território começou a Guerra Colonial, a 4 de fevereiro de 1961?
explanation: The Colonial War began in Angola on 4 February 1961. Two other fronts opened later: Guinea in 1963 and Mozambique in 1964. Angola first, then Guinea, then Mozambique — that order is often tested.

promptPt: Quais foram as três frentes da Guerra Colonial?
options: Moçambique, Cabo Verde e São Tomé
explanation: The war was fought in Angola, Guinea and Mozambique. Goa and Macau were Portuguese territories but not war fronts. Brazil had been independent since 1822.

promptPt: Que territórios portugueses foram anexados pela Índia em 1961?
explanation: In 1961 India annexed Goa, Daman and Diu, ending more than four centuries of Portuguese presence in India. It happened the same year the war began in Angola, so 1961 is a heavy date. Macau stayed Portuguese until 1999.

promptPt: Quanto tempo durou a Guerra Colonial?
options: Cerca de vinte e oito anos
Cerca de quarenta e oito anos
explanation: The war lasted about thirteen years, from 1961 to 1974. It required long military service, consumed much of the state budget and pushed many young men to emigrate to avoid being called up. It ended only with the revolution of 25 April 1974.

promptPt: O que aconteceu a 25 de abril de 1974?
options: Foi aprovada a Constituição da República
Portugal aderiu à Comunidade Económica Europeia
O Movimento das Forças Armadas derrubou o Estado Novo
explanation: On 25 April 1974 the Armed Forces Movement (MFA) overthrew the Estado Novo, almost without violence. It ended 48 years of dictatorship and thirteen years of colonial war. This is the single most important date in modern Portuguese history.

promptPt: Que canção foi a senha para o início das operações do 25 de Abril?
explanation: "Grândola, Vila Morena", by José Afonso, played on Rádio Renascença at 00:20 and was the signal for the operations to start. It is still sung at protests and commemorations today. "A Portuguesa" is the national anthem — a different thing entirely.
source: historia.md §11; Centro de Documentação 25 de Abril (cd25a.uc.pt).

promptPt: Quem compôs e cantou «Grândola, Vila Morena»?
explanation: José Afonso, known as Zeca Afonso, wrote and sang "Grândola, Vila Morena". His songs were censored under the dictatorship, which is exactly why the MFA chose one of them as the signal. Grândola is a town in the Alentejo.

promptPt: Onde se rendeu Marcelo Caetano, a 25 de abril de 1974?
options: No Quartel do Carmo, em Lisboa
explanation: Caetano surrendered at the Carmo barracks in Lisbon to General António de Spínola. He then left the country and went into exile. The Largo do Carmo is still a place people visit for this reason.

promptPt: Porque é que o 25 de Abril se chama Revolução dos Cravos?
options: Porque os soldados puseram cravos vermelhos nos canos das espingardas
Porque os cravos eram o símbolo do partido no poder
Porque aconteceu na época da colheita dos cravos
Porque a bandeira nova tinha um cravo
explanation: People in Lisbon handed red carnations to the soldiers, who put them in the barrels of their rifles. The image became the symbol of a revolution made almost without bloodshed. That is why the red carnation is worn every 25 April.

promptPt: O que se realizou a 25 de abril de 1975, um ano depois da revolução?
options: O referendo sobre a entrada na Europa
As primeiras eleições livres, para a Assembleia Constituinte
A tomada de posse do primeiro Presidente eleito
A entrada em vigor da Constituição
explanation: Exactly one year after the revolution, Portugal held its first free elections, by universal, direct and secret suffrage, to choose a Constituent Assembly. That assembly then wrote the Constitution. Women voted on equal terms for the first time.

promptPt: O que marcou o 25 de novembro de 1975?
options: A adesão de Portugal à NATO
O fim do período revolucionário e a abertura à democracia parlamentar
explanation: 25 November 1975 ended the revolutionary period known as the PREC and opened the way to parliamentary democracy. The eighteen months between April 1974 and November 1975 were politically very unstable. After this date the country settled into the system it still has.

promptPt: Quando entrou em vigor a atual Constituição da República Portuguesa?
explanation: The Constitution was approved on 2 April 1976 and entered into force on 25 April 1976, the second anniversary of the revolution. 23 July 1976 is a third date — the first constitutional government taking office. Approval, entry into force, government: three different moments.
source: historia.md §11; Assembleia da República, Constituição da República Portuguesa.

promptPt: Quem foi o primeiro Presidente da República eleito em democracia, em 1976?
explanation: Ramalho Eanes was elected President in 1976, the first under the new Constitution. Mário Soares formed the first constitutional government the same year and only became President later. Spínola was a general of 1974, not an elected president.

promptPt: Quem formou o primeiro governo constitucional, a 23 de julho de 1976?
explanation: Mário Soares formed the first constitutional government on 23 July 1976. He is one of the central figures of Portuguese democracy and later signed the treaty taking Portugal into Europe. Eanes was President, Soares was Prime Minister — two different jobs at the same time.

promptPt: Como se chama o feriado nacional de 25 de abril?
explanation: 25 April is the *Dia da Liberdade*, Freedom Day. 1 May, the day after, is *Dia do Trabalhador*, celebrated freely in Portugal for the first time in 1974. Both dates belong to the same spring.

promptPt: O que se celebra a 10 de junho?
options: O Dia de Portugal, de Camões e das Comunidades Portuguesas
explanation: 10 June is Portugal Day, and its full name honours the poet Luís de Camões and Portuguese communities abroad. The date is the anniversary of Camões's death. It is the national day proper, and it is celebrated in a different city each year.

promptPt: Qual foi a primeira antiga colónia portuguesa em África a tornar-se independente, em 1974?
explanation: Guinea-Bissau became independent on 10 September 1974, a few months after the revolution. The others followed in 1975: Mozambique in June, Cape Verde in July, São Tomé and Príncipe in July, Angola in November. Guinea-Bissau is the one that stands alone in 1974.

promptPt: Em que data se tornou Angola independente?
explanation: Angola became independent on 11 November 1975, the last of the African territories, after the Alvor Agreements signed in January of that year. 25 June 1975 is Mozambique and 5 July 1975 is Cape Verde; 28 November 1975 is the day East Timor declared independence. Angola is the last of the African territories in the sequence — that is the detail to remember.

promptPt: O que aconteceu a Timor-Leste depois de declarar a independência em 1975?
options: Foi invadido pela Indonésia e só restaurou a independência em 2002
explanation: East Timor declared independence on 28 November 1975 and was invaded by Indonesia days later, on 7 December. It only restored its independence on 20 May 2002. Today it is a member of the CPLP, the community of Portuguese-speaking countries.

promptPt: Em que ano foi Macau entregue à China?
explanation: Macau was handed over to China in 1999, which marked the end of the Portuguese empire. It was the last territory administered by Portugal outside Europe. Note the contrast: 1961 India, 1974–75 Africa, 1999 Macau.

promptPt: Quem são os «retornados»?
options: Os emigrantes que voltaram de França nos anos 80
As pessoas que regressaram das antigas colónias para Portugal
Os soldados que voltaram da Primeira Guerra Mundial
Os exilados políticos que voltaram depois de 1974
explanation: About half a million people came back from the former colonies to Portugal in 1975 and 1976; they are called *os retornados*. Absorbing so many people at once was a huge social and economic challenge for a country of nine million. The word is still used in everyday conversation.

promptPt: Onde foi assinado, a 12 de junho de 1985, o Tratado de Adesão de Portugal às Comunidades Europeias?
options: No Mosteiro dos Jerónimos, em Lisboa
explanation: The Accession Treaty was signed on 12 June 1985 at the Jerónimos Monastery in Lisbon. The venue was chosen deliberately: it is the monument of the age of Discoveries, so the symbolism was Portugal opening to the world again. Signature in 1985, membership in 1986.

promptPt: Quem era primeiro-ministro quando Portugal assinou o Tratado de Adesão, em 1985?
explanation: Mário Soares was Prime Minister and signed the treaty in 1985. He had also formed the first constitutional government in 1976, and later served as President. He is the name most associated with Portugal's European path.

promptPt: Em que data se tornou Portugal membro das Comunidades Europeias?
explanation: Portugal became a member on 1 January 1986, on the same day as Spain. The treaty had been signed in June 1985, but membership began the following January. The other two dates belong to Schengen and to the euro.
source: historia.md §13; União Europeia, ficha do país «Portugal».

promptPt: Que país aderiu às Comunidades Europeias no mesmo dia que Portugal?
explanation: Spain joined on the same day, 1 January 1986. Both countries had recently left dictatorships, and joining Europe was seen as a way of securing their new democracies. Greece had joined earlier, in 1981.

promptPt: Quando entraram em circulação as notas e as moedas de euro em Portugal?
explanation: Portugal has been in the euro area since 1 January 1999, but the notes and coins only came into people's hands on 1 January 2002. The currency existed on paper first and in your pocket three years later. Older people still convert prices into the old currency in their heads.

promptPt: Qual era a moeda portuguesa antes do euro?
explanation: The Portuguese currency before the euro was the *escudo*, replaced by euro notes and coins in 2002. The peseta was Spanish and the cruzeiro Brazilian. You may still hear older people say "contos", an old way of counting escudos.

promptPt: Coloca por ordem cronológica: Aljubarrota, São Mamede, Restauração da Independência, Implantação da República.
options: Aljubarrota, São Mamede, Implantação da República, Restauração da Independência
São Mamede, Aljubarrota, Restauração da Independência, Implantação da República
São Mamede, Restauração da Independência, Aljubarrota, Implantação da República
Implantação da República, São Mamede, Aljubarrota, Restauração da Independência
explanation: The order is 1128, 1385, 1640, 1910. Ordering questions are common in citizenship tests because they show whether you understand the story, not just isolated dates. Anchor yourself on the four centuries: twelfth, fourteenth, seventeenth, twentieth.

promptPt: Qual destas datas é a mais antiga?
options: O Tratado de Lisboa que reconheceu a independência
explanation: Alcanizes is 1297, Tordesillas 1494, Zaragoza 1529 and the Treaty of Lisbon 1668. Alcanizes is the oldest and the only one about the land border with Spain; the other three are about overseas territory or independence. Grouping treaties by what they were for makes them easier to remember.

promptPt: Qual destas afirmações sobre a história recente de Portugal é correta?
options: A Constituição atual foi aprovada durante o Estado Novo
Portugal aderiu à Comunidade Económica Europeia antes do 25 de Abril
A democracia foi restaurada em 1974 e Portugal aderiu à Europa em 1986
A Guerra Colonial terminou antes da chegada de Marcelo Caetano ao poder
explanation: The sequence is: 1974 revolution, 1976 Constitution, 1986 accession to the European Communities. Caetano came to power in 1968, while the war was still going on, and it only ended with the revolution. Getting this order right is the backbone of the modern history topic.

promptPt: Porque é que a história e os símbolos nacionais entraram no processo de nacionalidade portuguesa?
options: Porque a Constituição de 1976 sempre o exigiu
Porque é uma regra da União Europeia desde 1986
Porque o Regulamento da Nacionalidade de 2006 já o previa
Porque a Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026 passou a exigir que se conheça suficientemente a língua, a cultura, a história e os símbolos nacionais
explanation: Article 6(1)(c) of the Nationality Law, as amended by Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026 of 18 May 2026, requires applicants to show sufficient knowledge of the Portuguese language and culture, of history and of the national symbols. Note that the detailed rules — how the test works, how many questions, what pass mark — had still not been published when this bank was written. Study the subject, not a format that does not officially exist yet.
source: regulamento.md §3 e §7; Lei Orgânica n.º 1/2026, artigos 6.º e 4.º.
